questions.question:
Which statements are true about the Sprint Goal?
(choose the best two answers)

choices.label: A
choices.text: Sprint Goals give Developers flexibility and creativity on how to implement functionality during the Sprint.
choices.explanation: The Sprint Goal offers Developers the flexibility to determine how to achieve the set objective.

choices.label: B
choices.text: The use of Sprint Goals is optional in the Scrum Framework.
choices.explanation: Sprint Goals are a mandatory part of the Scrum Framework.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Sprint Goals often change during the Sprint as new insights emerge during the work.
choices.explanation: The Sprint Goal is meant to remain stable throughout the Sprint to provide focus and direction.

choices.label: D
choices.text: During Sprint Planning, the Scrum Team crafts a Sprint Goal based on an objective that the Product Owner would like to achieve that Sprint.
choices.explanation: During Sprint Planning, the Scrum Team collaborates to create a Sprint Goal based on a specific objective defined by the Product Owner.

questions.question:
A Developer from the Scrum Team is always missing the Daily Scrum. She feels that if she is doing her job well, it does not matter whether she attends or not. The other Developers on the team have not done anything about it. As the Scrum Master how should you respond to this situation?
(choose the best answer)

choices.label: A
choices.text: Ask the Developers, what value they get by having the Daily Scrum with all team members present and what might go wrong if all Developers do not attend.
choices.explanation: It encourages the team to understand the importance of the Daily Scrum and to collectively address the issue, fostering team ownership and accountability.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Teach the Developers how to deal with this situation by attending the Daily Scrum yourself.
choices.explanation: It does not empower the team to solve their own problems.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Talk to the Developer who is missing the Daily Scrum and ask her to always attend the Daily Scrum.
choices.explanation: It does not promote team self-management.

choices.label: D
choices.text: You do not intervene. The Developers own the Daily Scrum, so they should deal with any issues with attendance.
choices.explanation: As a Scrum Master, it is essential to facilitate understanding and proper execution of Scrum practices.

questions.question:
Where should the Daily Scrum be held according to the Scrum Guide?
(choose the best answer)

choices.label: A
choices.text: Around the Scrum Board
choices.explanation: Although a Scrum board can be helpful, Scrum does not prescribe any specific tool or physical location for the Daily Scrum. The Developers decide where and how it happens.

choices.label: B
choices.text: In the coffee corner to confirm this is an informal gathering
choices.explanation: The Daily Scrum is a focused event intended for Developers to plan the next 24 hours. Holding it in an informal or distracting environment like a coffee corner can undermine its purpose.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Wherever the Developers think is best
choices.explanation: The Scrum Guide states that the Daily Scrum should be held at the same time and place each day as decided by the Developers, to reduce complexity.

choices.label: D
choices.text: In a room where management can listen
choices.explanation: The Daily Scrum is for the Developers. Management listening in can inhibit open communication and violates the self-management principle.

choices.label: E
choices.text: In the room that is reserved by the Scrum Master
choices.explanation: The Scrum Master does not control the logistics of the Daily Scrum. The Developers are responsible for determining time and place.

questions.question:
What conditions are most likely occurring if you feel you need a "Quality Assurance and Release Readiness Sprint"?
{choose the best three answers)

choices.label: A
choices.text: The Definition of Done is weak or incomplete, allowing technical debt to accumulate.
choices.explanation: A weak Definition of Done allows technical debt to accumulate, indicating poor quality assurance.

choices.label: B
choices.text: You are following Scrum and the concept of a Hardening Sprint.
choices.explanation: Hardening Sprints are not part of standard Scrum.

choices.label: C
choices.text: The Developers find it nearly impossible to create a valuable, useful product Increment in a Sprint.
choices.explanation: It shows the difficulty in producing a valuable increment within a Sprint, indicating readiness issues.

choices.label: D
choices.text: The Definition of Done is not being met every Sprint.
choices.explanation: Not meeting the Definition of Done every Sprint shows a lack of proper quality checks.

choices.label: E
choices.text: Scrum has been modified in an acceptable manner to introduce "Quality Assurance and Release Readiness Sprints".
choices.explanation: Introducing "Quality Assurance and Release Readiness Sprints" is not an acceptable modification in Scrum.

questions.question:
What does the Scrum Team commit to each Sprint?
(choose the best three answers)

choices.label: A
choices.text: Increasing velocity
choices.explanation: Increasing velocity is not a commitment; it is a by-product of continuous improvement.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Seeking stakeholder feedback
choices.explanation: Seeking stakeholder feedback is encouraged but not defined as a formal commitment in Scrum.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Working towards the Sprint Goal
choices.explanation: Working towards the Sprint Goal is the primary commitment.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Upholding transparency.
choices.explanation: Transparency is essential for Scrum’s empirical process control.

choices.label: E
choices.text: Having the Product Owner available to the Developers on a daily basis.
choices.explanation: It is not always feasible for the Product Owner to be available daily.

choices.label: F
choices.text: Getting all the forecast work in the Sprint Plan done.
choices.explanation: Delivering the forecasted work supports achieving the Sprint Goal, which is the Sprint commitment.

questions.question:
You are the Scrum Master of a Scrum Team that has one Developer who disagrees with team decisions. Their disagreements are becoming disruptive and slowing progress. The Developer often returns to earlier team decisions and re-opens the issue.
What are two ways to go about this problem? 
(choose the best two answers)

choices.label: A
choices.text: You organize an offsite team building activity to establish a foundation of trust. You observe whether the problem persists after the offsite activity.
choices.explanation: While team-building activities are beneficial, they do not directly address the specific issue of re-opening decisions.

choices.label: B
choices.text: You take the Developer aside to express your concem over their disagreements and tell them to act as a team player and to comply with the team’s decision.
choices.explanation: It might not foster a collaborative environment and could be seen as imposing authority.

choices.label: C
choices.text: At the Sprint Retrospective you observe whether the topic is raised. If it does not happen, you check on how comfortable everybody is with the way team decisions are made
choices.explanation: The Sprint Retrospective is the appropriate time to discuss and address team dynamics and decision-making processes.

choices.label: D
choices.text: You go to the Human Resources department and ask them to have a conversation with the Developer based on the issues the team has raised
choices.explanation: Escalating to HR should be a last resort after team-level solutions have been exhausted.

choices.label: E
choices.text: To every team member expressing this concem you suggest raising this with the full team. You offer to help initiate the conversation but not to resolve the concern yourself.
choices.explanation: It encourages the team to collectively address and resolve issues, promoting self-management.

questions.question:
During a Sprint Review, the Product Owner determines that she is going to release the current Increment to production. The stakeholders ask to stop the Sprint to react more quickly to the user feedback that is expected after this release. The Product Owner prefers to continue the Sprint to make progress with the next release. You facilitate a discussion on how to proceed.
What are two acceptable results of this discussion?
(choose the best two answers)

choices.label: A
choices.text: Stop sprinting and let the Developers work on new customer requests as they arise.
choices.explanation: Stopping the Sprint goes against the principles of maintaining a timebox and predictable cadence.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Continue sprinting but allow customer feedback to change the Sprint Goal within the Sprint.
choices.explanation: Changing the Sprint Goal mid-Sprint undermines the focus and commitment of the team.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Continue sprinting but shorten the Sprint length to allow for shorter feedback loops.
choices.explanation: Shortening the Sprint length allows for quicker feedback loops and responsiveness to user feedback.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Continue sprinting and include the customer feedback in the Product Backlog.
choices.explanation: Including customer feedback in the Product Backlog ensures that it will be considered in future planning without disrupting the current Sprint.

questions.question:
A Scrum Master colleague of yours wants some guidance on what to do in the following situation. During the Daily Scrum, one Scrum Team member, who is a key central figure in the organization, drags on and on about things which actually are interesting but not relevant for the Daily Scrum, day after day. What are two suggestions you would offer to your colleague?
(choose the best two answers)

choices.label: A
choices.text: You suggest passing a token around. The person holding the token has the floor to speak for an allotted amount of time.
choices.explanation: While passing a token can help manage speaking time, it doesn't address the root cause of the problem.

choices.label: B
choices.text: You suggest coaching the Developers to help them find a way to solve the problem, and own the solution.
choices.explanation: Coaching the team to find their solution promotes self-management and ownership.

choices.label: C
choices.text: You suggest using a timer, to limit the time each person can speak at the Daily Scrum
choices.explanation: Using a timer can feel restrictive and may not address the underlying issue of focus.

choices.label: D
choices.text: You suggest taking the person aside and asking them what they believe the key outcomes are for the Daily Scrum. Effectively coaching them to help create focus during the Daily Scrum
choices.explanation: It involves directly addressing the individual and helping them understand the purpose of the Daily Scrum, fostering better focus and adherence to the agenda.

choices.label: E
choices.text: You contact the team member's Line Manager and raise this as an impediment to the Manager, and ask that they resolve this matter.
choices.explanation: Escalating to a Line Manager is unnecessary for a team-level issue and does not promote team self-management.

questions.question:
A Scrum Team selected a Product Backlog item during Sprint Planning. However, at the end of the Sprint the work does not meet the Definition of Done. What two things should happen with this incomplete Product Backlog item?
(choose the best two answers)

choices.label: A
choices.text: Review the item, add the done part of the estimate to the velocity and create a Story for the remaining work
choices.explanation: Splitting the estimate is not a practice in Scrum and can lead to inaccuracies.

choices.label: B
choices.text: The item is not included in the Increment for this Sprint.
choices.explanation: An item that does not meet the Definition of Done should not be included in the Increment.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Only the stakeholders decide over acceptance of undone work and whether to release it
choices.explanation: The stakeholders do not decide on the acceptance of incomplete work; it is the responsibility of the Scrum Team to ensure only done items are considered.

choices.label: D
choices.text: It is put on the Product Backlog for the Product Owner to decide what to do with it
choices.explanation: The incomplete item should be returned to the Product Backlog for the Product Owner to decide the next steps.

questions.question:
You are a Scrum Master helping to establish five Scrum Teams that will be building a product. You discuss with them the high level of integration that the product Increment will require by the end of their first Sprint. It is a highly anticipated product, both by consumers and by the organization. Of the options raised by the future Scrum Team members, which option do you encourage?
(choose the best answer)

choices.label: A
choices.text: In the first Sprint, integration is less important. The goal is to deliver business value. Functionality that is not integrated with the work of other Scrum Teams by the end of a Sprint is still reviewed to assess its potential business value. It can still be released at the Product Owner's discretion, and silent consent of the stakeholders.
choices.explanation: Integration is crucial from the start to avoid technical debt and ensure all components work together seamlessly.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Each Scrum Team provides a separate Increment with the functionality added by the individual team. The Sprint Review is used to identify the work needed to integrate with the other Scrum Teams. This work is then added to the Product Backlog.
choices.explanation: Separate Increments can lead to integration challenges and inconsistencies.

choices.label: C
choices.text: All Scrum Teams agree on a shared Definition of Done that describes all work needed to deliver an Increment that is the integrated sum of the work from all Scrum Teams.
choices.explanation: A shared Definition of Done ensures that all work is integrated and meets the same quality standards, allowing for a cohesive and releasable product Increment.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Each Scrum Team delivers done Increments in its own area of responsibility. Upon functional acceptance at the Sprint Review, the code is isolated for future stabilization. The release date is adjusted according to the expected work and time of such integration phase.
choices.explanation: Delaying integration can create significant issues and risks closer to the release date.

questions.question:
What are acceptable ways a Scrum Master may work to ensure Scrum is understood and enacted?
(choose the best three answers)

choices.label: A
choices.text: Schedule group training about Scrum.
choices.explanation: Group training helps spread knowledge about Scrum across the team and organization.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Educate stakeholders and customers about Scrum.
choices.explanation: Educating stakeholders and customers ensures everyone involved understands Scrum practices and values.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Arrange one-on-one coaching sessions where concems the Scrum Master has identified can be discussed.
choices.explanation: One-on-one coaching sessions allow for personalized guidance and addressing specific concerns.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Require senior management to mandate that all teams in the organization must follow and enact Scrum.
choices.explanation: Mandating Scrum does not ensure understanding or proper enactment; it requires buy-in and understanding from the team.

choices.label: E
choices.text: Hold longer, more in-depth retrospectives with formal learning as part of the retrospective.
choices.explanation: While retrospectives are important, they should remain focused and timeboxed; formal learning sessions should be separate.

questions.question:
You are a Scrum Master entering an organization that wants to “evolve” their product development to Scrum. The organization's teams are organized into component teams. This means that teams address one single application layer only (for example, front end, middle end, back end, and interfaces).
You introduce the concept of feature teams, where teams have the skills to work on multiple layers throughout a Sprint and deliver working software every Sprint. 
What are two things you take into consideration when moving away from component teams toward feature teams?
(choose the best two answers)

choices.label: A
choices.text: Feature teams will require time to become productive as people from the different layers and components become accustomed to working and delivering unified functionality together, as one Scrum Team
choices.explanation: Transitioning to feature teams will initially require time for team members to adapt to new ways of working across multiple layers.

choices.label: B
choices.text: With feature teams, it is easier to calculate and compare the productivity per team. Incentives on productivity are likely to speed up the transition to feature teams, and therefore the adoption of Scrum.
choices.explanation: Productivity comparisons and incentives are not the main focus in Scrum.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Productivity, in terms of lines of code or story points, will probably suffer during the transition, although even then delivery of business value is still likely to increase.
choices.explanation: Productivity metrics might show a temporary decline during the transition, but the overall delivery of business value is expected to improve.

choices.label: D
choices.text: You cannot do Scrum without feature teams. Do not continue adopting Scrum until teams are reorganized in feature teams.
choices.explanation: Scrum can be implemented with component teams, though feature teams are more aligned with Scrum principles.

questions.question:
Five new Scrum Teams have been created to build one product. A few of the Developers ask the Scrum Master who will coordinate the work between the different Scrum Teams. 
What should the Scrum Master do?
(choose the best answer)

choices.label: A
choices.text: Visit the five Scrum Teams each day to facilitate alignment and synchronization of their Sprint Backlogs,
choices.explanation: The Scrum Master should not be doing the coordination work for the teams; the teams should self-organize.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Collect the Sprint tasks from the teams at the end of their Sprint Planning and merge that into a consolidated plan for the entire Sprint.
choices.explanation: Merging Sprint tasks into a consolidated plan undermines team autonomy.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Teach the Product Owner to work with the lead developers on ordering Product Backlog in a way to avoid too much technical and development overlap during a Sprint.
choices.explanation: While the Product Owner should work on ordering the Product Backlog, lead developers should not be given special roles outside the team.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Teach them that it is their responsibilty to form Scrum Teams with the skills and knowledge to create an Increment by the end of every Sprint.
choices.explanation: It emphasizes the responsibility of Scrum Teams to be self-managing and to have the skills and knowledge to create a potentially shippable Increment by the end of every Sprint.

choices.label: E
choices.text: Advise the teams to reduce interdependence by working in separate branches and organizing a specific Sprint every four development Sprints to manage integration.
choices.explanation: Working in separate branches can create silos and delay integration.

questions.question:
How does the Scrum Master serve the Scrum Team?
(choose the best two answers)

choices.label: A
choices.text: The Scrum Master facilitates Scrum events as requested or needed
choices.explanation: Facilitating Scrum events is a core responsibility of the Scrum Master.

choices.label: B
choices.text: The Scrum Master resolves every impediment that the Developers run into.
choices.explanation: While the Scrum Master helps remove impediments, resolving every impediment is not solely their responsibility; the team should also be empowered to address issues.

choices.label: C
choices.text: The Scrum Master coaches the Scrum Team and the organization how to work empirically.
choices.explanation: Coaching the team and the organization on empirical work supports continuous improvement and adherence to Scrum values.

choices.label: D
choices.text: The Scrum Master never intervenes in matters of the Scrum Team, but allows them to maximize their autonomy and freedom.
choices.explanation: The Scrum Master sometimes needs to intervene to support the team and ensure Scrum practices are followed correctly.

questions.question:
What are two signs that a Scrum Team is self-managing? 
(choose the best two answers)

choices.label: A
choices.text: The Developers always know the status of the assigned work needed to deliver the tasks committed in the Sprint Plan.
choices.explanation: Knowing the status of assigned work is not necessarily indicative of self-management; it's more about how the team manages and resolves their work.

choices.label: B
choices.text: The Scrum Team can resolve conflicts and continue working.
choices.explanation: The ability to resolve conflicts independently is a key sign of a self-managing team.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Management understands the team’s daily tasks at all times.
choices.explanation: Management understanding daily tasks is not relevant to a team's self-management.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Creativity flourishes and new possibilities are explored.
choices.explanation: Creativity and the exploration of new possibilities indicate a team that is self-directed and empowered.

questions.question:
In an environment where user acceptance testing is required before the Increment can be put into production, a development manager proposes to have user acceptance testing done every third Sprint, because the feedback from the user acceptance tests are disrupting work in Sprints. 
Is this a good idea? 
(choose the best answer)

choices.label: A
choices.text: Yes, the Scrum Team is a self-managing team.
choices.explanation: Self-management does not justify practices that reduce transparency and delay feedback.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Yes, the Scrum Team needs stability in the Sprint.
choices.explanation: While stability is important, it should not come at the cost of delayed feedback.

choices.label: C
choices.text: No, the increment will not be transparent and the feedback loop is too long
choices.explanation: Delaying user acceptance testing reduces transparency and elongates the feedback loop, which is contrary to the principles of Scrum that emphasize short feedback cycles and frequent inspection and adaptation.

choices.label: D
choices.text: It depends on what is stated in their Definition of Done.
choices.explanation: Even if the Definition of Done allows it, it does not align with Scrum best practices.

questions.question:
A Scrum Team is struggling over the fact that not all Developers work full time and that other Developers regularly work from home. To solve the difficulties in aligning daily, at the Sprint Retrospective two Developers suggest having the Daily Scrum every three days, when everyone is in the office.
What would be three key concems if the frequency of the Daily Scrum were to be lowered?
(choose the best three answers)

choices.label: A
choices.text: The Scrum Master loses the ability to update the Gantt chart properly, thereby obscuring the Scrum Master's tracking of Sprint progress.
choices.explanation: Updating a Gantt chart is not part of Scrum practices.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Impediments are raised and resolved more slowly which might impact productivity and progress.
choices.explanation: Less frequent Daily Scrums slow down the identification and resolution of impediments.

choices.label: C
choices.text: The Product Owner cannot accurately report progress about the state of the forecasted work to the stakeholders.
choices.explanation: The Product Owner’s ability to report progress should not depend on the frequency of Daily Scrums but on regular communication and updates.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Less progress information will be shared, causing the plan for the Sprint to become inaccurate and transparency over progress toward the Sprint Goal is reduced.
choices.explanation: Less frequent updates reduce transparency and can lead to an inaccurate Sprint plan.

choices.label: E
choices.text: Opportunities to inspect and adapt the Sprint Backlog are reduced. Re-aligning is bound to become even more difficult,
choices.explanation: Fewer opportunities to inspect and adapt make it harder to stay aligned with the Sprint Goal.

questions.question:
You are a Scrum Master employed by the IT department. The IT manager considers adopting Scrum for a new project. He wonders however, what the value is in having all team member attend this meeting called “Daily Scrum” every day. The organization already has its employ attending so many mandatory meetings.
What are two outcomes of the Daily Scrum you inform him about, to express the importance the Daily Scrum?
(choose the best two answers)

choices.label: A
choices.text: during the Daily Scrum, the Developers need to update the Scrum board with their current status and progress, at a task level. This is crucial to ensure that the IT manager can go up to the room at any time and view the team’s actual progress
choices.explanation: The Daily Scrum is not for updating the Scrum board for management's viewing.

choices.label: B
choices.text: During the Dally Scrum the Developers will bring up problems that are hindering their progress, and for which they have no means to resolve, this provides an opportunity to resolve those impediments.
choices.explanation: The Daily Scrum helps identify and resolve impediments that are blocking progress.

choices.label: C
choices.text: The Developers wit produce a status report indicating what each individual has done the past working day, and how much time that has taken. The accumulates reports will support discussing how the Sprint went at the Sprint Review meeting twill provide detailed insights into the accuracy of estimates versus actual time spent, which can be used to create better estimates at the subsequent Sprint Planning meeting
choices.explanation: Generating detailed status reports is not the purpose of the Daily Scrum.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Through the short daily alignment of the Daly Scrum the Developers build ang Improve a shared understanding of the most important work to be undertaken in the next 24 hours to achieve the best possible progress toward the Sprint Goal Tis day opportunity to Inspect and adapt will enable the Developers to tackle any unforeseen circumstances that might otherwise disrupt the team’s progress
choices.explanation: The Daily Scrum provides a daily opportunity to inspect and adapt, ensuring alignment and progress towards the Sprint Goal.

choices.label: E
choices.text: The bally Scrum serves for the Developers to report to you. as @ Scrum Master all updates on the tasks of the Sprint, as registered in the Sprint Backlog. You can then use the team's updates to plan their work for the next day, making sure that every team members assigned the right tasks
choices.explanation: The Daily Scrum is not for reporting to the Scrum Master but for the team to plan and coordinate their work.

questions.question:
You are the Scrum Master for four teams working from the same Product Backlog. Several of the Developers come to you complaining that work identified for the upcoming two Sprints will require full time commitment from Phil, an external specialist. As the Scrum Master what should you do to solve this upcoming problem?
(choose the best answer)

choices.label: A
choices.text: Prepare the Sprint Backlogs each day for the teams so Phil can spend some time in each team.
choices.explanation: Preparing Sprint Backlogs for the teams undermines their self-management.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Allocate Phil to one team per Sprint, so that over four Sprints every team will have had the support it requires.
choices.explanation: Rotating Phil may not be the most efficient use of his time or the teams' needs.

choices.label: C
choices.text: As needed, consult with the Developers on how they want to manage this problem and help them implement their preferred solution.
choices.explanation: Consulting with the Developers allows for a collaborative approach to managing the issue and finding a practical solution that the team supports.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Ask Phil for a plan to hire and train additional people in his domain, and in the meantime work with the Product Owner and Developers to re-prioritize the work so that tasks not depending on Phil can be done first.
choices.explanation: While hiring and training additional people can be a long-term solution, it does not address the immediate problem effectively.

questions.question:
Scrum Master is a management position because the Scrum Master is accountable for the following three management activities :
(choose the best three answers)

choices.label: A
choices.text: The way Scrum is understood and enacted within the organization.
choices.explanation: The Scrum Master is responsible for ensuring that Scrum is understood and enacted correctly.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Removing organizational impediments that limit the team's progress and productivity.
choices.explanation: The Scrum Master helps remove impediments that affect the team's productivity.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Managing the project plan and the project deliverables
choices.explanation: Managing the project plan and deliverables is not the responsibility of the Scrum Master.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Managing the Scrum process.
choices.explanation: The Scrum Master manages the Scrum process to ensure it is followed properly.

choices.label: E
choices.text: Reporting on the performance of a team
choices.explanation: The Scrum Master does not focus on reporting team performance; this is more aligned with the Product Owner.

choices.label: F
choices.text: Managing the capacity and utilization of the Developers.
choices.explanation: Managing the capacity and utilization of Developers is not the Scrum Master's role; the team self-manages this aspect.

questions.question:
A Scrum Team consists of Developers working from globally distributed locations. Organizing the Scrum events requires conferencing tools that are not easily available within the organization. The Developers propose doing a Daily Scrum only on Tuesdays. Which are the most appropriate responses for their Scrum Master? 
(choose the best two answers)

choices.label: A
choices.text: Coach the Developers on why a daily frequency is important as an opportunity to update the Sprint Plan and how it helps the team organize work toward achieving the Sprint Goal.
choices.explanation: Coaching the Developers on the importance of the daily Scrum helps them understand its value in updating the Sprint Plan and organizing work towards the Sprint Goal.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Have the Developers vote to make sure there is consensus within the team.
choices.explanation: Voting on the frequency does not address the underlying importance of daily updates.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Help the Developers understand that lowering the frequency of communication will only increase the feeling of disconnect between the team members.
choices.explanation: Lowering the frequency of communication can increase the feeling of disconnect between team members, affecting collaboration and alignment.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Acknowledge and support this self-managing team’s decision.
choices.explanation: Supporting this decision undermines the principles of Scrum, which emphasize daily communication for effective progress.

questions.question:
The relationship between the Product Owner and the Developers has degraded over time. The Developers are growing increasingly angry with the Product Owner for changing the requirements all the time and not being available enough. The Product Owner is angry with the Developers for changing requirements during implementation. 
What guidance should the Scrum Master offer? 
(choose the best answer)

choices.label: A
choices.text: Ask each person's functional manager to instruct their employees that they must collaborate better, or be removed from the team.
choices.explanation: Involving functional managers does not promote team self-management and collaboration.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Take everyone to a 2-day off-site event to relax and re-align. It is liberating to take people's minds away from work.
choices.explanation: An off-site event may not address the root cause of the issue.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Ask for a project manager or other external resource to mediate and temporarily take over for the Product Owner.
choices.explanation: Bringing in an external resource can undermine the roles and responsibilities within the Scrum framework.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Address why requirements change during the Sprint Retrospective. Ask the Developers and the Product Owner to talk about why the requirements are changing and consider the impact on value during this discussion.
choices.explanation: Addressing why requirements change during the Sprint Retrospective and discussing the impact on value encourages transparency and collaboration between the Product Owner and Developers.

questions.question:
You are the Scrum Master for three Scrum Teams working on the same product. There is a single Product Backlog that all three Scrum Teams select from. Management is eager to improve the productivity of the teams and wants to standardize velocity across all three teams so that they can see how each team is delivering value. 
When responding to management, which two statements are appropriate?
(choose the best two answers)

choices.label: A
choices.text: Incentivizing teams based on velocity can boost the Scrum Team's motivation to create more value.
choices.explanation: Incentivizing based on velocity can lead to undesirable behaviors and does not necessarily increase value.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Standardizing velocity across teams can help with understanding which teams are creating more value
choices.explanation: Standardizing velocity across teams does not help in understanding value creation.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Velocity has no direct relationship with value.
choices.explanation: Velocity is not directly related to value; it is a measure of the amount of work a team can complete in a Sprint.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Velocity is the amount of business functionality that a Scrum Team creates in a Sprint. It is unique to that team and used as an input to Sprint Planning
choices.explanation: Velocity is unique to each team and is used as an input for Sprint Planning, not for comparing across teams.

questions.question:
Which two statements are true regarding the nature of large-scale product development with Scrum?
(choose the best two answers)

choices.label: A
choices.text: A well-structured Product Backlog can minimize and often eliminate Developers working on multiple Scrum Teams during a Sprint.
choices.explanation: A well-structured Product Backlog helps minimize the need for Developers to work on multiple teams, reducing context switching and increasing focus.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Scrum Team members must be working full time on a team.
choices.explanation: Team members do not necessarily need to be full-time to be effective.

choices.label: C
choices.text: A person working on multiple Scrum Teams at the same time is often less productive than when that person can focus on the Sprint Backlog of a single Scrum Team.
choices.explanation: Focusing on one team's Sprint Backlog allows for greater productivity compared to working across multiple teams.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Changes to the core Scrum framework are needed to be successful with Scrum at large scale.
choices.explanation: Changes to the core Scrum framework are not required for large-scale Scrum implementation.

questions.question:
Which two of these situations best demonstrate that a Scrum Team is self-managing?
(choose the best two answers)

choices.label: A
choices.text: Management is invited to the Daily Scrum for a progress update and subsequently works with the Scrum Master to optimize the plan for the next day.
choices.explanation: Management involvement in Daily Scrums undermines team autonomy.

choices.label: B
choices.text: The Scrum Team invites the right external people to the Sprint Planning to help them create a complete and detailed Sprint Backlog before the meeting timebox expires.
choices.explanation: Inviting external people to Sprint Planning should not be about completing a detailed Sprint Backlog but about collaboration.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Developers collaboratively select and re-plan their work during the Sprint.
choices.explanation: Self-managing teams collaboratively select and re-plan their work during the Sprint.

choices.label: D
choices.text: The Developers create their own Sprint Backlog, reflecting all work that is part of the Definition of Done.
choices.explanation: Self-managing teams create their own Sprint Backlog, including all work needed to meet the Definition of Done.

choices.label: E
choices.text: The Developers are strictly working within the boundaries of their function description, and are handing off work in a timely fashion to the other members within the team.
choices.explanation: Strictly working within functional boundaries limits cross-functional collaboration.

questions.question:
Towards the end of Sprint Planning, the Product Owner and the Developers have not been able to reach a clear, mutual understanding about the highest order Product Backlog items. Because of this, the Developers could not figure out how many Product Backlog items they could forecast for the upcoming Sprint. The Product Owner did make it clear what business objective he is hoping to achieve with this Sprint. 
Which of the following two actions would you support?
(choose the best two answers)

choices.label: A
choices.text: The Developers forecast the most likely Product Backlog items to meet the business objective and create a Sprint Backlog based on a likely initial design and plan. Once the timebox for the Sprint Planning event is over, they start the Sprint and continue to analyze, decompose, and create additional functionality during the Sprint.
choices.explanation: The Developers can start the Sprint with an initial design and plan, continuing to refine the Product Backlog items during the Sprint.

choices.label: B
choices.text: The team splits up and everybody takes as much time as they need to study the Product Backlog items first. The Product Owner should be available to answer individual questions. The group reconvenes when all team members are better prepared and restart the Sprint Planning meeting before the Sprint can star.
choices.explanation: Splitting up and reconvening disrupts the team’s collaboration and the Sprint Planning process.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Ifall agree, they can continue the Sprint Planning meeting as a team past its timebox, until an adequate number of Product Backlog items are well enough understood for the Developers to make a complete forecast. Then start the Sprint.
choices.explanation: Extending the Sprint Planning timebox ensures a mutual understanding and an adequate number of well-understood Product Backlog items.

choices.label: D
choices.text: They discuss in the upcoming Sprint Retrospective why this happened and what changes will make it less likely to recur.
choices.explanation: Discussing the issue in the Sprint Retrospective does not solve the immediate problem of starting the Sprint.

questions.question:
A multi-national company is using Scrum for product development of their five major products. What alternatives should the company consider to decide how many Product Owners are needed for these five products?
(choose the best two answers)

choices.label: A
choices.text: There is one Product Owner for each product (five in total). Each Product Owner may delegate to others for specific value, capabilities, and functionality within their product. The five Product Owners share and align work via Product Backlog.
choices.explanation: Having one Product Owner per product ensures clear accountability and alignment across products.

choices.label: B
choices.text: There is one Product Owner responsible for all five products. This person may delegate work to others for specific value, capabilities, and functionality within each product to scale their accountability.
choices.explanation: The Product Owner can delegate part of the work to others while keeping the accountability.

choices.label: C
choices.text: There is one Product Owner for all five products. This person may not delegate work to others for specific value, capabilities, and functionality, given these are all the Product Owner's individual responsibility
choices.explanation: A single Product Owner without delegation may not be able to manage all requirements effectively.

choices.label: D
choices.text: There are as many Product Owners as needed to analyze, document, and explain expectations and requirements with all Scrum Teams.
choices.explanation: The tasks are only related to documentation, not all Product owner’s responsibilities.

questions.question:
One Scrum Team is developing a product. They track how much software they produce as velocity. Their current velocity is 18 units of done work. A second team will be added to work on the same product. 
What is the most likely impact on the velocity of the original team?
(choose the best answer)

choices.label: A
choices.text: Their velocity is likely to be not affected and stay at 18.
choices.explanation: It is unlikely that the original team’s velocity will remain unaffected by the addition of a new team.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Their velocity is likely to decrease and be lower than 18.
choices.explanation: Adding a second team is likely to introduce dependencies and coordination challenges, which can initially decrease the original team’s velocity.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Their velocity is likely to increase and be higher than 18.
choices.explanation: Increasing velocity with a new team is not typically immediate due to the need for integration and collaboration.

questions.question:
Scrum requires a Definition of Done. Which phrases describe the purpose of the Definition of Done?
{choose the best three answers)

choices.label: A
choices.text: It is a checklist to inspect whether the Developers have performed their tasks by the end of a Sprint.
choices.explanation: It is not just a checklist for task completion.

choices.label: B
choices.text: It serves to track the percent completeness of a Product Backlog item during the Sprint.
choices.explanation: It does not track percent completeness.

choices.label: C
choices.text: It provides a template for the documentation of the product Increment.
choices.explanation: It is not a template for documentation.

choices.label: D
choices.text: It creates transparency into the state of the Increment when it is inspected at the Sprint Review.
choices.explanation: The Definition of Done creates transparency into the state of the Increment.

choices.label: E
choices.text: During the Sprint it helps the Developers identify the work remaining for an Increment to be ready for release by the end of a Sprint.
choices.explanation: It helps Developers identify remaining work for the Increment to be release-ready.

choices.label: F
choices.text: It guides the Developers when creating a forecast at the oh Planning,
choices.explanation: It guides Developers in creating a forecast during Sprint Planning.

questions.question:
Which two options describe how project budgeting and financial forecasting work in Scrum?
(choose the best two answers)

choices.label: A
choices.text: Several Sprints may be funded as a single release, with the result of each Sprint being releasable product.
choices.explanation: It’s common in Scrum to fund several Sprints at once and still ensure a releasable Increment after each Sprint.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Scrum does not align with traditional accounting practices. The financial department needs to be given a fixed cost per Sprint per team.
choices.explanation: Providing a fixed cost per team per Sprint helps align with traditional financial controls.

choices.label: C
choices.text: The only funding is for the run cost (time and materials) of the Scrum Teams, so no budgeting process is needed.
choices.explanation: Budgeting processes are still necessary to manage costs and ensure value delivery.

choices.label: D
choices.text: It is ideally revisited as frequently as each Sprint to ensure value is being delivered for the investment spent.
choices.explanation: Frequent revisiting of budgeting ensures value is being delivered for the investment.

questions.question:
You have just been hired as a Scrum Master by a company new to Scrum. The company wants to use Scrum to build a new product that was conceived by the product management department. You will be the Scrum Master of two new teams that will build a first version of the product. The product management department assigns two new Product Owners, but wants more advice about the required participation with the new Scrum Teams. 
Which two suggestions would you offer?
(choose the best two answers)

choices.label: A
choices.text: Two Product Owners are necessary, one for each Scrum Team. They report to an overarching chief Product Owner.
choices.explanation: Having two Product Owners can lead to confusion and misalignment.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Having one Product Owner will improve the clarity of accountability to the teams and to the product management department.
choices.explanation: Having one Product Owner improves accountability and clarity for the teams and the product management department.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Each Scrum Team has a separate Product Backlog, holding each team's assigned requirements
choices.explanation: Separate Product Backlogs for each team can create silos and reduce the overall visibility of requirements.

choices.label: D
choices.text: A single Product Backlog should be maintained holding all requirements for the new product
choices.explanation: Maintaining a single Product Backlog ensures that all requirements are visible and prioritized across both Scrum Teams.

questions.question:
Your organization has announced a release to its user base three Sprints from now. To be able to include all functionality in the release, work needs to accelerate. The Product Owner puts some testing from the Definition of Done on hold for the next three Sprints, while adding a generic item to the Product Backlog to resolve this in a future release. The Developers object that this will lead to technical debt. 
Select two ways that explain the impact of technical debt to the Product Owner.
(choose the best two answers)

choices.label: A
choices.text: Ageneric Product Backiog item is not good enough. The amount of technical debt will have to be calculated and estimated much more precisely, so the total amount of extra work that needs to be budgeted is well known,
choices.explanation: Calculating the exact amount of technical debt is impractical and does not address the immediate impact.

choices.label: B
choices.text: As development progresses and functionality is added upon the reduced Definition of Done, unknown errors will creep in. The system becomes more difficult to stabilize. Work for the actual release as well as future releases will be slowed down in unpredictable ways.
choices.explanation: Putting off testing from the Definition of Done leads to technical debt and can result in a more difficult and unstable system over time.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Releasing the version creates false assumptions about the actual state of the system. This is likely to result in interruptions during future Sprints in order to react to unforeseen problems arising from not having met the Definition of Done.
choices.explanation: Releasing an incomplete version creates false assumptions about the system’s state, leading to future interruptions and unforeseen problems.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Feature development of a next release is not allowed to start as long as there is technical debt from the current release. The Product Owner should first accept this impact before the Definition of Done can be reduced.
choices.explanation: Technical debt can exist alongside new feature development; the focus should be on managing it effectively.

questions.question:
You are the Scrum Master for a Scrum Team whose Daily Scrum is scheduled to start at 10:00 each day. Developers routinely turn up late, and once everyone has assembled, the Daily Scrum starts. By then it is typically 4 to 5 minutes later than scheduled. Other meetings in the organization typically allow 4 to 5 minutes for people to transport within the building. Some Developers complain that it is now hard to achieve the purpose of the Daily Scrum within the timebox, since there is only 10 or 11 minutes left after waiting for people to show up. 
The Developers ask for your advice.
(choose the best answer)

choices.label: A
choices.text: To incentivize showing up on time, you tell the Developers that when people come late to the Daily Scrum, they will pay a small fee.
choices.explanation: Imposing a fee can create a punitive environment and does not address the root cause.

choices.label: B
choices.text: You turn the question back to the Developers and ask what they think should be done to ensure their Daily Scrum is effective and meets its purpose.
choices.explanation: Turning the question back to the Developers allows them to take ownership and find a solution that works for the team, fostering self-management and accountability.

choices.label: C
choices.text: You suggest that when someone shows up late they cannot join that day's Daily Scrum,
choices.explanation: Excluding latecomers may cause them to miss important information and does not foster team unity.

choices.label: D
choices.text: You escalate this issue to management since you are responsible for ensuring Scrum is understood and enacted.
choices.explanation: Escalating to management undermines team self-management.

choices.label: E
choices.text: You suggest an experiment: moving the event to a time that better suits the team.
choices.explanation: It may not address the specific issue of tardiness and could disrupt established routines.

questions.question:
What are two effective ways the Scrum Team can manage these high-security concerns?
(choose the best two answers)

choices.label: A
choices.text: During the Sprint Retrospective, the Scrum Team assesses how to add these expectations to the Definition of Done so every future Increment will live up to these requirements. If needed they can work with external specialists to better understand the requirements
choices.explanation: Incorporating security concerns into the Definition of Done ensures all future Increments meet these requirements.

choices.label: B
choices.text: They should be managed by a separate specialist team in a parallel Sprint, so they can be specifically resolved through an improved application design without hindering functional development.
choices.explanation: A separate team working in parallel can lead to integration challenges and siloed knowledge.

choices.label: C
choices.text: They are discussed, determined, and documented in parallel Sprints to not disturb the actual feature development. Once analyzed, they should be applied to the work already done before further feature development can continue.
choices.explanation: Postponing the analysis can delay addressing critical security issues.

choices.label: D
choices.text: The impact of these security concerns on past and future work needs to be determined before new Sprints can start. A list of security-related Product Backlog items needs to be passed on to the Product Owner before starting the next Sprint.
choices.explanation: Separating security from functional development can create coordination problems.

choices.label: E
choices.text: They are added to the Product Backlog and addressed throughout the next Sprints, combined with creating the business functionality in those Sprints, no matter how small that business functionality.
choices.explanation: Addressing security concerns alongside business functionality in future Sprints integrates security into the development process.

questions.question:
A Scrum Team has been working together for nine Sprints. A new Product Owner comes in, unsure about his responsibilities. As the Scrum Master you have observed how the functional and business insights of the Developers have grown over the past Sprints. The Product Owner however is relatively new to the company and to the product. 
What are two activities you would direct the new Product Owner towards focusing on?
(choose the best two answers)

choices.label: A
choices.text: You advise the Product Ovmer to start building a good relationship with the stakeholders of the product. On-going interaction with them is important to regularly align with changing organizational or market expectations. The Product Owner is also expected to invite the appropriate stakeholders to the Sprint Review
choices.explanation: Building a relationship with stakeholders ensures alignment with their expectations and market changes.

choices.label: B
choices.text: You inform the Product Owner that, in today’s highly competitive markets, it is important that the Developers are updated on changing business priorities on a daily basis. It is why Scrum has this daily meeting. At this Daily Scrum the Developers can adapt to the changes in scope without delay.
choices.explanation: Daily updates on changing business priorities are not the purpose of the Daily Scrum and can cause unnecessary disruptions.

choices.label: C
choices.text: You tell the Product Owner to make sure that there are no ambiguities or possible misunderstandings in the items on the Product Backlog when they are handed over to the Scrum Team. This is best done by capturing the functional requirements during an analysis phase, resulting in documents that are considered as the working product of such analysis sprints.
choices.explanation: Relying solely on documented requirements does not promote collaboration and can lead to misunderstandings.

choices.label: D
choices.text: You advise the Product Over to rely on others in the Scrum Team and the stakeholders to formulate the Product Backlog, as they are the ones that are up to speed. By questioning them and working with them the Product Owner will quickly become more productive.
choices.explanation: Collaborating with the Scrum Team and stakeholders helps the Product Owner quickly gain necessary insights and knowledge.

questions.question:
An important aspect of Scrum are timeboxes. Select two ways in which timeboxing reinforces the creation of value.
(choose the best two answers)

choices.label: A
choices.text: Timeboxes help everyone focus on the same problem at the same time.
choices.explanation: Timeboxes focus the team on solving the problem within the allotted time, promoting efficiency.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Scrum Teams can determine on their own how much overtime is acceptable for a timebox- generally expressed as a percentage of the timebox.
choices.explanation: Overtime is not a recommended practice in Scrum and can lead to burnout.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Timeboxing assures that a Product Owner does not interrupt the Developers during a Sprint.
choices.explanation: Timeboxing alone does not prevent the Product Owner from interrupting the team.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Timeboxes encourage the people who are closest to the problem to create the best possible result in the time allotted, given the current context.
choices.explanation: Timeboxes encourage the team to produce the best possible result within the given time, fostering creativity and problem-solving.

questions.question:
At the seventh Sprint Review, the stakeholders seem disappointed and angry. When asked about it,they say the product being built will not meet their needs and will cost more than they anticipated spending. 
What factors may have led to this?
(choose the best three answers)

choices.label: A
choices.text: The Project Management Office (PMO) and its project managers have not been adequately engaged, causing the project plan to become inaccurate.
choices.explanation: Engagement with the PMO is not relevant to Scrum practices.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Changes to the project plan were not adequately documented and shared. The change request procedure was not diligently followed.
choices.explanation: Change request procedures are not part of Scrum.

choices.label: C
choices.text: The stakeholders have not been using the Sprint Reviews to actively engage, and inspect and evaluate progress.
choices.explanation: Stakeholder engagement during Sprint Reviews is crucial for alignment and feedback.

choices.label: D
choices.text: The Scrum Master has not ensured transparency.
choices.explanation: Transparency is essential for managing expectations and progress.

choices.label: E
choices.text: The stakeholders were not allowed to enter the development area, or be present at the Daily Scrum.
choices.explanation: Stakeholders are not required to attend Daily Scrums.

choices.label: F
choices.text: The Product Owner has not been interacting frequently with the stakeholders and kept them aware of the progress of the project.
choices.explanation: Frequent interaction with the Product Owner ensures stakeholders are kept informed and engaged.

questions.question:
You are the Scrum Master for four Scrum Teams working from the same Product Backlog Several of the Developers come to you complaining that work identified for the upcoming two Sprints will require full time commitment from Stella, an external specialist who is not a member of any of the four Scrum Teams. 
What would you consider acceptable solutions for the problem?
(choose the best three answers)

choices.label: A
choices.text: Have the Developers re-order the Product Backlog so Stella can serve one team full-time in a Sprint.
choices.explanation: Re-ordering the Product Backlog to serve one team at a time may not be efficient.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Organize a release Sprint in which Stella can thoroughly check and complete all the work done in her domain before considering the work releasable.
choices.explanation: A release Sprint with a focus on Stella’s work can delay overall progress.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Ask Stella for a plan to hire and train additional people in her domain, and in the meantime work with the Product Owner and Scrum Teams to re-prioritize the work so that tasks not depending on Stella can be done first.
choices.explanation: Hiring and training additional people addresses the long-term need for Stella’s expertise.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Create a team with Stella and identify people from the Scrum Teams to temporarily work in Stella's domain to learn to better serve the existing teams.
choices.explanation: Temporarily forming a new team may disrupt the existing teams.

choices.label: E
choices.text: Developers with an interest in Stella’s domain could volunteer to take on this work in their respective Scrum Teams.
choices.explanation: Developers with interest in Stella’s domain can learn and provide support.

choices.label: F
choices.text: Merge the Scrum Teams into one large Scrum Team for the next two Sprints, When the need for Stella's expertise is over, the teams can separate again.
choices.explanation: Merging and then separating the teams can cause instability.

choices.label: G
choices.text: Investigate whether additional techniques or frameworks for scaling Scrum would be appropriate for these Scrum Teams.
choices.explanation: Investigating additional scaling techniques or frameworks can help manage dependencies and coordination.

questions.question:
Your organization always stresses the importance of on-time delivery and reliability. A manager has detected that your team’s progress is too slow. They feel that your team’s velocity needs to be 10% higher. The organization expects you, as the Scrum Master, to make it happen. 
How do you respond?
(choose the best two answers)

choices.label: A
choices.text: You explain how a Scrum Team uses the velocity of a Sprint primarily to forecast work for the next Sprint, not to perfectly predict future productivity. You refer management to the Product Owner for all information concerning the progress of development
choices.explanation: It explains the proper use of velocity and directs management to the Product Owner for progress information.

choices.label: B
choices.text: You educate management that itis the Scrum Team's responsibility to improve their velocity. You invite management to the next Sprint Retrospective to brainstorm on how they can improve
choices.explanation: Inviting management to the Sprint Retrospective can undermine team autonomy.

choices.label: C
choices.text: You tell management that this is not your accountability in Scrum. You direct them to the Product Owner to determine whether the forecast is accurate.
choices.explanation: Dismissing management’s concerns without addressing the root cause can lead to further issues.

choices.label: D
choices.text: You help management understand that it typically takes a few Sprints for a team to gradually increase the velocity up to the level expected. Meanwhile you present this to the team as a challenge and a company goal, leaving it however up to them to figure out exactly how to achieve this.
choices.explanation: Setting a challenge without addressing the root causes of low velocity may not be effective.

choices.label: E
choices.text: You inform management of organizational impediments that prevent the Scrum Team from being more productive. You enlist their help to remove these impediments
choices.explanation: Enlisting management’s help to remove impediments supports the team’s productivity and improvement.

questions.question:
How should requirements be distributed when multiple Scrum Teams work on the same product?
(choose the best answer)

choices.label: A
choices.text: The Scrum Teams pull in work from a shared Product Backlog in agreement with the Product Owner and the other teams.
choices.explanation: Having teams pull work from a shared Product Backlog ensures alignment and collaboration with the Product Owner and other teams.

choices.label: B
choices.text: The Product Owner decides by providing each team with its own Product Backlog.
choices.explanation: Separate Product Backlogs can create silos.

choices.label: C
choices.text: The Scrum Team with the highest velocity pulls items from an overall Product Backlog first.
choices.explanation: Prioritizing based on velocity does not ensure the highest value work is done.

choices.label: D
choices.text: They must be selected from one Product Backlog in such a way that each Scrum Team has an equal volume of requirements per Sprint.
choices.explanation: Equal volume of requirements does not guarantee value delivery.

questions.question: True or False: When scaling Scrum it is important to have multiple Scrum Teams working from one Product Backlog ?

choices.label: A
choices.text: True
choices.explanation: Having multiple Scrum Teams working from one Product Backlog ensures alignment and consistency in delivering a valuable product.

choices.label: B
choices.text: false
choices.explanation: It contradicts the principle of having a unified Product Backlog.

questions.question:
During Sprint Planning, Developers work with the Product Owner to create a forecast for the Sprint. A forecast is a selection of Product Backlog items that the Developers believe are possible to get done by the end of the Sprint. 
Select two things that explain what done means.
(choose the best two answers)

choices.label: A
choices.text: All work for which enough expertise and skills are present in the Scrum Team.
choices.explanation: Expertise and skills alone do not define “done.”

choices.label: B
choices.text: All work to create an Increment that is ready for acceptance testing by the Product Owner.
choices.explanation: Acceptance testing is part of the Definition of Done.

choices.label: C
choices.text: All work to create an Increment that is ready for testing
choices.explanation: Testing is included in the Definition of Done, but it’s not the only aspect of being “done.”

choices.label: D
choices.text: Having an Increment that could be released to end users.
choices.explanation: Having an Increment that could be released to end users meets the Scrum principle of delivering potentially shippable product increments.

choices.label: E
choices.text: All work performed meets the Definition of Done.
choices.explanation: Meeting the Definition of Done ensures the work is complete and of high quality.

questions.question:
You are a Scrum Master and one of the Developers approaches you and says: Every Sprint we are not completing regression testing for all of the selected Product Backlog items in the Sprint, but regression testing is part of the Definition of Done. We have discussed with the Product Owner and during the Sprint we decided to change the Definition of Done to remove regression testing. 
Which two actions are appropriate in this situation?
(choose the best two answers)

choices.label: A
choices.text: Agree with altering the Definition of Done, if both the Developers and Product Owner agree.
choices.explanation: Agreeing to alter the Definition of Done without considering the impact on quality is not advisable.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Ask the Developers and the Product Owner if removing regression testing from the Definition of Done allows the team to produce useful and valuable Increments at the end of every Sprint?
choices.explanation: Discussing whether removing regression testing allows for useful and valuable Increments ensures the focus on quality.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Ask the Developers and the Product Owner what problem they are going to solve by altering the Definition of Done during the Sprint to remove regression testing. Will this raise transparency or improve quality?
choices.explanation: Understanding the problem behind altering the Definition of Done promotes transparency and quality improvement.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Disagree with the decision and tell them that having a stringent Definition of Done is important for the quality of the product, and they need to follow it.
choices.explanation: Enforcing a stringent Definition of Done without understanding the team’s challenges may not be effective.

questions.question:
In the Sprint Review, one of the stakeholders highlights the money spent this year, and that due to market changes, the funding may run out. An argument follows this statement, with raised voices and strong emotional statements. 
As a Scrum Master, what are your two best options?
(choose the best two answers)

choices.label: A
choices.text: Encourage the stakeholders to focus on delivering the highest value items for the next Sprint.
choices.explanation: Focusing on delivering the highest value items helps prioritize the work despite funding concerns.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Argue that the Scrum Team needs to be kept busy while the funding is confirmed.
choices.explanation: Keeping the team busy without a clear focus on value is not productive.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Ask for a short break for people to calm down and be objective.
choices.explanation: Taking a break to calm down allows for more objective and productive discussions.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Defend the budget, asking the stakeholders to support the funding of the work.
choices.explanation: Defending the budget without addressing concerns can escalate conflicts.

choices.label: E
choices.text: It is the Product Owner's meeting, so do nothing.
choices.explanation: The Scrum Master should facilitate productive discussions, not remain passive.

questions.question:
A Scrum Team has been using the Daily Scrum to report Sprint progress to the Product Owner, because the Product Owner wants to track what every Developer is working on every day. 
What is the best thing for the Scrum Master to do?
(choose the best answer)

choices.label: A
choices.text: Nothing. The Product Owner can continue to track progress at the Daily Scrum.
choices.explanation: Using the Daily Scrum for reporting progress undermines its purpose.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Ask the Product Owner to stop attending the Daily Scrum.
choices.explanation: Excluding the Product Owner from the Daily Scrum can reduce collaboration.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Start attending the Daily Scrum so that whenever the Developers have a conflict with the Product Owner, the Scrum Master can resolve the conflict.
choices.explanation: The Scrum Master’s role is to coach, not to resolve conflicts during the Daily Scrum.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Coach the Product Owner and the Developers on the purpose of Scrum events and let them figure out how to deal with this situation.
choices.explanation: Coaching the Product Owner and Developers on the purpose of Scrum events helps them understand and properly use the Daily Scrum.

questions.question:
A few members of the Scrum Team discuss work that is not being done. Some say it is part of the Definition of Done, others say it is not. After an hour of angry discussion, someone starts making personal insults and anger levels rise. 
What is the best action for the Scrum Master to take? 
(choose the best answer)

choices.label: A
choices.text: End the discussion. Make the call whether the work is or is not part of the Definition of Done. Identify who is involved in the conflict and decide on their further presence on the Scrum Team,
choices.explanation: Making a unilateral decision undermines team collaboration.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Conduct a session to help the Scrum Team resolve the conflict and create a uniform Definition of Done. Remind the other members of the Scrum Team that conflicting ideas are natural, but making it personal does not help.
choices.explanation: Conducting a session to resolve the conflict and create a uniform Definition of Done promotes collaboration and mutual understanding.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Take the people involved aside. Ask them to resolve the situation outside of the Scrum Team, if required through their managers. The goal is to maintain stability in the team.
choices.explanation: Resolving conflicts outside the team can prevent addressing the underlying issues.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Defuse the conflict. Take the Definition of Done and tell the other members of the Scrum Team how to interpret it, so they can autonomously decide whether the debated work is or is not part of it.
choices.explanation: Telling the team how to interpret the Definition of Done does not foster autonomy.

questions.question:
After some small experiments with Scrum, your company decides to do a complete project with Scrum. As Scrum Master, you have been invited to the project kick-off meeting with IT and product management. The Product Owner asks how many Sprints IT will need to first figure out architecture and Infrastructure issues. 
What are two options to explain how such work is managed using Scrum?
(choose the best two answers)

choices.label: A
choices.text: You educate the Product Owner to add this work to the Product Backlog to Uphold transparency. Ask the Developers to plan work during the first several Sprints to estimate these items, while also creating some business functionality in these early Sprints,
choices.explanation: Adding work to the Product Backlog and planning it transparently ensures visibility and proper prioritization.

choices.label: B
choices.text: You expiain that product management should not worry about such typical IT work, You inform them that you will assure that the team members reach out to the right people within the IT organization when needed. During each Sprint Planning event they will Keep the Product Owner updated about the adational effort it will ake for that Sprint, That effort will come on top of the effort for the forecasted functional development,
choices.explanation: Relying solely on IT for architecture and infrastructure does not align with Scrum’s collaborative approach.

choices.label: C
choices.text: You thank product management for understanding that these efforts indeed require effort and budget. You confirm that architecture and infrastructure are best addressed before starting Scrum, but that the exact budget is difficult to calculate upfront. You say you will organize this work in timeboxed Sprints of no more than 30 days to limit risk and be transparent toward product management on the actual progress
choices.explanation: Organizing work in timeboxed Sprints without integrating functionality can delay value delivery.

choices.label: D
choices.text: You explain that technical risks are best controlled when architecture and Infrastructure emerge alongside the development of functionality. The additional advantage is that business value is created faster and sooner.
choices.explanation: Addressing technical risks alongside functionality promotes balanced progress.

questions.question:
Which of the following affect the outcome of a Sprint?
(choose all that apply)

choices.label: A
choices.text: The complexity of the requirements.
choices.explanation: Complex requirements may lead to uncertainty in delivery and impact Sprint outcomes.

choices.label: B
choices.text: The skills and working relationships of the people on the Scrum Team(s).
choices.explanation: A team's skills and collaboration directly influence the quality and speed of delivery.

choices.label: C
choices.text: The complexity of the problem being solved.
choices.explanation: The more complex the problem, the more likely it will affect the team's ability to deliver.

questions.question:
What can the Scrum Value of openness easily impact?
(choose the best answer)

choices.label: A
choices.text: Collaboration.
choices.explanation: Collaboration is influenced by multiple values, not openness alone.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Product quality.
choices.explanation: Product quality is also driven by commitment, focus, and technical practices.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Employee satisfaction
choices.explanation: Employee satisfaction depends on many factors beyond openness.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Time to market.
choices.explanation: Time to market is a result of team efficiency, planning, and delivery discipline.

choices.label: E
choices.text: Stakeholder trust
choices.explanation: Stakeholder trust requires transparency, delivery, and consistent communication—not just openness.

choices.label: F
choices.text: All of the above.
choices.explanation: Openness impacts collaboration, product quality, employee satisfaction, time to market, and stakeholder trust.

questions.question: True or False: Using Scrum ensures that adding more resources to a project proportionally increases the value delivered.

choices.label: A
choices.text: True
choices.explanation: Adding more resources does not proportionally increase value delivered, due to factors like team dynamics

choices.label: B
choices.text: False
choices.explanation: Adding more resources does not proportionally increase value delivered, due to factors like team dynamics

questions.question:
During the Sprint Retrospective, the newest developer says that his perspective and ideas have been ignored by the rest of the Developers throughout the Sprint. 
What Scrum values are touched here?
(choose the best three answers)

choices.label: A
choices.text: Focus
choices.explanation: Focus relates to staying on goals, not how team members treat each other.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Courage
choices.explanation: It takes courage to speak up when you feel ignored.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Transparency
choices.explanation: Transparency refers to visibility of work and progress, not interpersonal behavior.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Openness
choices.explanation: Openness means welcoming all ideas and perspectives within the team.

choices.label: E
choices.text: Commitment
choices.explanation: Commitment is about dedication to goals, not necessarily team interactions.

choices.label: F
choices.text: Respect
choices.explanation: Respect is essential to value every team member’s input, regardless of seniority.

questions.question:
Creating a forecast for a Sprint tends to run more smoothly when the Product Backlog items that are discussed are well understood and actionable. 
Which approach would you recommend to ensure well understood and actionable Product Backlog items at Sprint Planning?
(choose the best answer)

choices.label: A
choices.text: The Developers use some time in each Sprint to analyze, estimate and design high-ordered Product Backlog items.
choices.explanation: Using time in each Sprint to analyze, estimate, and design high-ordered Product Backlog items ensures they are well understood and actionable.

choices.label: B
choices.text: The Product Owner works with the stakeholders to prepare Product Backlog items outside of the Sprint so the Developers will not be disrupted
choices.explanation: The Product Owner preparing items outside of the Sprint without involving the team can lead to misunderstandings.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Aseparate Scrum Team of business analysts and testers analyze high-ordered requirements one Sprint ahead of development.
choices.explanation: A separate team of business analysts and testers working ahead is not aligned with Scrum principles.

choices.label: D
choices.text: The analysts on the Scrum Team document high-ordered Product Backlog items during a Sprint when they are not busy working on the forecast.
choices.explanation: Analysts documenting items during a Sprint can disrupt the focus on current work.

questions.question:
In the Daily Scrum, the Product Owner applauds every Developer who moves a Sprint Backlog item to completion. The Product Owner wants to encourage the Developers to make progress visible on the burn-down chart. 
Select the two best options for the Scrum Master to take.
(choose the best two answers)

choices.label: A
choices.text: Take the opportunity to create more energy and team spirit and encourage everyone to participate in the applause.
choices.explanation: Encouraging applause can distract from the purpose of the Daily Scrum.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Tell the Product Owner your concerns about how his behavior may impact the Developers, and ask him to stop attending the Daily Scrum for some time.
choices.explanation: The Product Owner’s behavior may impact the team’s dynamics, and addressing it directly helps maintain focus.
